title: story-brief
description: One defect the Inspector found, written as a pre-planning artifact. A BRIEF IS NOT A STORY AND NOTHING EXECUTES ONE: it carries intent, evidence and a severity, it is not an approved plan, and it never becomes one on its own. A human plans it into a story artifact through l5-plan's interview, and that interview is where the mandate is conferred — so there is nothing here to refuse, because the coordinator has no path that runs a brief. It stands alone rather than being nested inside the inspector's own envelope because it is two things at once: the payload an outbox entry carries, and the document a later story fetches one of and validates on its own. THE PATHS A BRIEF CARRIES ARE BARE REPOSITORY-RELATIVE PATHS, and the reason is mechanical rather than stylistic: the sync command writes one searchable marker per entry of the payload's paths, and the query command searches for the marker of a bare repository-relative path, so a path carrying a line number would be filed under a marker no scoped query ever asks for and the dedupe this whole mechanism exists for would silently never match. The file:line citations that are the evidentiary standard live in the body, where they are read by a person and not searched for by a script. WHAT AN ENTRY IS FILED UNDER is the kind, the category, the sorted paths and the slug, and title, body, severity and confidence are deliberately outside it: they are the parts a model rephrases between runs, and an identity that drifts is a duplicate filed on every inspection.

title.description: What the defect is, in one line, for a human scanning a tracker. Prose, and deliberately not part of what the brief is filed under: two inspections of one defect will phrase it differently, and filing on the phrasing would file it twice.

slug.description: A short kebab-case name for the defect, derived by the rule prompts/inspector.md states so that two inspections of the same defect derive the same one. It is the part of the identity that distinguishes two findings of the same category against the same paths, so a brief without one has no stable name to be filed under and is dropped.

body.description: The case for the finding: what is wrong, the evidence for it cited as file:line, what the consequence is, and what would resolve it. This is where line-level evidence lives, because paths above may not carry it.

category.description: What kind of defect this is. Part of the identity, because it is a classification the Inspector makes from the code rather than a phrasing it chooses.

severity.description: How bad the consequence is if this is left alone: 3 is a defect that produces wrong behaviour or silently disables a check, 2 is one that costs correctness of understanding or will produce a defect under a foreseeable change, 1 is one worth fixing when the code is next open. Defined by consequence and not by effort or by confidence, and a finding may not be 3 unless its confidence is high. It is payload rather than identity, because it is a judgement a second inspection may rate differently about one defect.

confidence.description: How sure the Inspector is that this is real, as an axis separate from severity: a high-consequence guess and a certain triviality are different things and collapsing them into one number loses both.

effort.description: Roughly how much work resolving this is: S is a contained edit, M is a story, L is work that should be split before it is planned.

workflow.description: The workflow this brief should be planned under, named exactly as a definition under workflows/ is named. A plain string rather than an enum, deliberately: the acceptable names are the definitions the harness holds, so a third workflow becomes selectable by shipping a definition rather than by editing this schema. A name the harness does not define is dropped and named by the module rather than by this shape.

paths.description: The repository-relative paths this finding is about, bare and carrying no line number, no column and no selector — see the reason in this schema's own description. Optional, because a finding about the absence of something has no path to name; a brief carrying none is filed under an identity with no paths, and no scoped query will find it.

not_in_scope.description: What a story planned from this brief should deliberately leave alone, in the Inspector's own words. Optional, and advisory: nothing reads it, and the human planning the brief decides what it is worth.
